preview: Today, we're talking about something big: the idea of a singularity in AI, a moment when machines might outpace us. One well-known tech leader says it's already happening. Another says it's landing very soon. Other experts aren't so sure. As you listen, think about this: when someone makes a big claim about the future, how do you know if you should believe them?
comment_1: In this first part, listen for two big quotes from two very famous people in AI. Notice exactly what each one says, and how sure they sound.
comment_2: So, one tech leader says the singularity is already here. Another says it's coming this year. But that's just what two people believe. Next, listen for what the actual research says. Does the evidence agree with them?
comment_3: So the real picture is more mixed than the bold claims suggest. AI is amazing at some things, and surprisingly bad at others. And one huge survey of researchers puts good odds on something similar, but only much later, and even they don't fully agree with each other. Now, let's look at two reasons why this debate is so hard to settle.
comment_4: So part of the problem is that people can't agree on what singularity even means. And a personal claim from one leader is a very different kind of evidence from a big survey. With all that in mind, here's the story in one line.
